title: Cantonese-Style White Stir-Fry Sauce
description: Pale chicken broth, poached garlic and white pepper give this translucent sauce a clean, delicate finish.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: unsalted dry drinking sherry
ingredients.note: Use drinking sherry, without added salt.

ingredients.name: table salt
ingredients.note: Fine table salt, about 590 mg sodium per 1/4 teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/16 tsp total.

steps.title: Infuse the broth
steps.text: Simmer {ch}, {ga}, {gi}, {sh} and {wp} covered for 5 minutes over low heat.

steps.title: Clarify the base
steps.text: Pass the liquid through a fine sieve into the skillet, pressing gently on the garlic. Add {salt} and {so} and return to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over chicken and steamed vegetables, shrimp, or mild white fish when you want the main ingredient to stand out.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/16 tsp table salt in place of 1/4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, replace sherry with water and leave out the white pepper. Nutrition includes the garlic before straining and the sherry before simmering. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 19 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 2.5 g total carbohydrate, 0.3 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 157 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 19 kcal, 0.6 g protein, 2.5 g total carbohydrate, 0.3 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 46 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
